sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Research completed with unresolved verification holds, not a buy recommendation: GP Eco is a rapidly expanding solar distribution/EPC/storage group, but reported profit growth is materially stronger than independently interpretable cash generation. At the 19 October 2026 official close of ₹395.65, current issued-share market value is ₹487.8285 crore. The 20 October cutoff was an NSE cash-market holiday, so no 20 October quote is invented. [S10, S11]
BQS, GQS (Growth Quality Score) and IAS are all NS. Known-weight coverage is 68%,45% and 10%; original-weight mathematical bounds are 3.04–5.92,2.60–7.55 and 1.60–9.70, not estimated scores or confidence intervals. Persistent weak cash conversion would cap a fully computable GQS at 5; it does not turn missing evidence into a 5. No score is ranking-eligible. [S1–S10]
The decisive evidence is the FY26 cash-flow statement: reported CFO₹29.3263 crore includes ₹35.5470 crore of short-term borrowing increase. Subtracting this financing movement produces a diagnostic negative ₹6.2207 crore, not an audited restatement. Moreover,₹14.5967 crore of ₹19.6999 crore reported cash comprises uncleared cheques. The audit's main opinion is unmodified, but its internal-control annex calls for stronger debtor/stock controls. [S1]
Strong counter-evidence exists: revenue grew 68.15%, normalized operating EBIT reached ₹57.7431 crore, the September credit rating improved, July capital was raised and specific new orders were disclosed. Those positives warrant continued research rather than an allegation of fraud/default. They do not establish current usable funds or attributable returns on new capital. An apparently 12.16× historical earnings quote therefore does not establish a bargain. [S1, S5, S7, S12–S15]

The cash-growth cap 5 is shown separately; governance≤3 and evidenced-funding-failure overrides do not apply because those findings were not made. None makes a missing aggregate scoreable. This distinguishes uncertain judgment from missing data and avoids pretending a 0.1-point ranking is meaningful.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The parent historically distributes solar inverters and modules, increasingly adding tracker supply, EPC, project services and battery-storage/inverter manufacturing through subsidiaries including Invergy and AN3 Techno, plus GPES Green and other project companies. Distribution monetizes supplier access, inventory, channel support and receivable financing; EPC monetizes engineering/execution milestones but consumes guarantees, advances and retention capital; manufacturing needs qualification, reliable output, working capital and warranty support. Economic models differ, so gross sales growth alone cannot establish common unit economics. [S1, S4, S5]
The rating's FY26 line items distribution ₹319.21 crore, EPC₹55.46 crore and BESS₹11.00 crore total ₹385.67 crore, aligning with parent revenue ₹385.6747, not consolidated ₹414.3842. Its prose must not be used to label that mix consolidated external revenue. Subsidiary turnovers are not added to group sales: for example Invergy ₹129.61 crore and GPES Green ₹66.05 crore include transactions potentially eliminated on consolidation. The group describes one reporting segment; no reliable external sales/elimination bridge by product is supplied in the reviewed material. [S1, S5]
Solar and storage demand offer opportunity, but there is no defensible bottom-up accessible-TAM share estimate from the disclosed data. Customer qualifications, cells/power-electronics sourcing, installed throughput, utilization and working-capital finance are the bottlenecks to test. A storage factory's nameplate GWh does not convert mechanically to sales without sell-through, pricing and cell cost. The research consequently models revenue/capital sensitivities rather than inventing unit sales from a headline national renewable target. [S4, S6]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
GP Eco has distribution relationships, delivery/service integration, an Invergy brand and an expanding product offering. These can reduce customer procurement friction, but supplier-held technology, contestable distribution rights and customer financing demands constrain pricing power. Historical RHP concentration is substantial: nine months to December 2023 top-ten suppliers 89.94%, largest 42.18%; top-ten customers 51.94%, largest 17.26%. These are old risk baselines, not invented FY26 concentrations. The FY23 supplier table also has a percentage/amount denominator inconsistency, so that percentage is not used as a decisive current input. [S4]
Three economically relevant comparators are used for mechanisms rather than unsupported stock rankings. Sungrow is an upstream inverter/storage technology manufacturer with a broader product/technology role than a local distributor; it illustrates what proprietary technology/service capability would have to demonstrate. Servotech is a partial equipment/inverter/charging comparator, not a matched revenue-mix substitute. Oriana Power's June 2026 discussion describes EPC/IPP and storage-related expansion; asset ownership/project financing makes its cash needs different. No synchronized peer market multiples or financial quality scores have been verified, and none is fabricated. [S22–S24]
Evidence that could upgrade MOAT includes repeated qualified wins, persistent realized margins after warranty losses, measurable distributor/customer retention, defensible intellectual property and returns on substantial reinvestment. A familiar supplier name, an order award or certification alone is insufficient. Current score 4 reflects contestability and absent demonstrated excess economics; it does not deny that a useful commercial franchise exists. Capacity growth can improve or dilute that franchise, depending on execution and the funding terms. [S1, S4, S6]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The safe financial model embeds FY21–FY26 parent revenue ₹46.4682,83.4476,101.2124,136.3375,240.0938 and 385.6747 crore. Its nominal five-year CAGR is 52.69%. The separately comparable reported consolidated series for FY24–FY26 is ₹138.4438,246.4348 and 414.3842 crore, a 73.01% two-year CAGR. FY26 group year-on-year growth is 68.15%. These are calculations from primary historical statements, not an organic-volume growth assertion. The FY23 consolidated comparative in the FY24 annual report was supplied for cash-flow comparison around Invergy's January 2024 acquisition, so it is not spliced into a longer group growth series. [S1–S4]
The numerical v 3.0 schedule would start at 9 for a genuinely comparable≥30% CAGR. It is not applied here because the underlying basis is unresolved: solar-equipment prices, distribution gross sales, new EPC/storage activities, acquired entities and group eliminations materially alter what a rupee of revenue means. No externally reconciled volume/price/acquisition/FX bridge or organic revenue alternative is available. This is why REV is NS, not 9 with an arbitrary small-base haircut, or 5 as a neutral placeholder. History/confidence caps do not repair absent comparability. [S1, S4, S5]
Actual awards provide cross-checks that activity is not purely promotional, but do not prove the entirety of group sales or collections. The two tracker awards total ₹115.4877503 crore; the EPC order is ₹13 crore including GST and cannot be added gross as future net sales; the inverter order is ₹18.23925 crore with a September deadline. Opening backlog, execution, cancellations and net closing backlog are ND. Claims of multi-fold FY27 growth remain management statements with unresolved FY26 guidance history. [S6, S12–S16]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Growth has required substantial financial resources: FY26 net PPE cash purchase ₹53.5723 crore plus CWIP₹8.1322 crore, receivables rising ₹130.8138 crore, and supplier advances ₹35.6560 crore at year-end. Customer advances rose to ₹59.4413 crore and payables to ₹140.4100 crore, both funding sources with associated delivery/payment obligations. They are not costless permanent equity. Partial ONWC defined as receivables+inventory+supplier advances−payables−customer advances is ₹87.5549 crore, versus ₹38.3399 crore a year earlier. This deliberately excludes other operating/tax accruals and is not presented as a complete audited ONWC reconciliation. [S1, S2]
CAP remains NS. Broad capital-return diagnostics include total group equity/NCI/debt, cash/deposit/property adjustments and show average/incremental ratios, but acquisitions, capital timing, advances, deposit restrictions and the boundary between growth/maintenance investment prevent attribution of new NOPAT to new capital. No unit/cohort economics resolves that gap. A reasoned nominal industrial capital-cost sensitivity would need debt costs, equity risk and the actual funding mix; the 15% equity hurdle is not silently used as WACC. No CAP conclusion is drawn merely because historical ROCE looks high. [S1, S5]
The June call described full 3 GWh capacity by September, FY27 capex above ₹150 crore and roughly ₹200 crore total Dasna investment, while also saying the hard capex phase was behind the company. Those statements need a dated reconciliation to completed, commissioned, qualified and revenue-producing assets. The model varies FY27 capex ₹80/150/175 crore, ONWC32%/26%/25% and growth/margins, explicitly as analytical paths rather than funded management forecasts. The bull path needs the largest early cash rescue, showing that fast growth can increase financing risk rather than automatically improve growth quality. [S6]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The promises-versus-delivery register is central. On 10 November 2025 management accepted the approximately ₹700–750 crore FY26/3× growth interpretation and described storage operations by January–February 2026. The June 2026 call reported first Dasna commercial operation 30 May, described a later full September phase, and said the earlier revenue target had always been ₹550–600 crore. Actual group revenue was ₹414.38 crore. Both the original and retrospective accounts are preserved rather than replacing one with the other. Management cited policy/input-cost-related deferrals; a reconciled order/revenue and capex bridge remains necessary. This supports EXEC4 and stewardship caution, not a finding of intent to deceive. [S16, S17, S6, S1]
Post-July promoter ownership was 59.42%;4,065,981 promoter shares were encumbered,55.5% of promoter holding and 32.98% of current equity. Lock-in 4,187,819 shares (33.97%) is a separate restriction. Pledges can amplify forced-sale exposure but do not themselves establish diversion or an inability to refinance. Actual July allotment 499,000 shares is used instead of larger EGM proposals. Potential fully diluted shares 15,390,450 include outstanding warrants and granted options, not the full merely authorized option pool. [S7, S8, S1]
The 12 May 2025 IPO-use certificate reports ₹27.1091 crore net proceeds utilized:₹12.45 crore working capital,₹7.60 crore investment in Invergy and ₹7.0591 crore general purposes. Its qualification states the subsidiary transfer remained unutilized by Invergy at 31 March 2025. Thus a parent-level utilization label did not prove plant commissioning or group expenditure. No IPO cash is counted again in the forward model. [S21]
The group disclosed large director-related loan flows, related receivables, remuneration and consulting fees. An NSE-query response describes a shareholder-approved ₹1,000 crore RPT envelope and Invergy becoming wholly owned 3 July 2025; this is the company's explanation, not independent legal clearance. Direction and closing balance reconciliation of loans needs clarification. Corporate guarantees ₹28.9233 crore are reviewed for location/overlap, not mechanically added to consolidated debt. A GST demand/penalty ₹0.32148 crore was contested; the final outcome is ND. Finance-leadership changes alone are not misconduct evidence. [S1, S18–S20]
The main auditor's opinion is unmodified, while the internal-control annex is explicitly qualified in its basis language and calls for stronger receivable/stock controls. That distinction is more informative than describing the entire audit as clean. Independent control-remediation and subsequent collections, plus consistent candid guidance, would improve the assessment. [S1]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Reported consolidated CFO FY24/FY25/FY26 is−₹6.0893/₹22.3319/₹29.3263 crore. The same cash statements include short-term borrowing movements−₹0.2327/₹19.8323/₹35.5470 crore in working capital. Removing those flows gives−₹5.8566/₹2.4996/−₹6.2207 crore, cumulative−₹9.5777 crore against group PAT₹60.5312 crore. Reported three-year CFO/PAT75.28% becomes diagnostic−15.82%. Borrowing movements can include noncash/acquisition effects; this is a warning and reconciliation request, not an audited substitute. CFO already reflects interest via PBT: the diagnostic FCF does not subtract interest twice. [S1–S3]
FY26 reported cash ₹19.6999 crore decomposes to ₹3.5778 bank,₹1.4663 hand,₹0.059 escrow and ₹14.5967 uncleared cheques. Sum differs by ₹0.0001 crore from presentation rounding. The conservative historical cash input ₹5.0441 excludes uncleared cheques, escrow,₹21.9582 crore noncurrent FDs and ₹1.0364 collateral until availability is evidenced. It is not a current cash assertion. Gross debt ₹108.9691 includes current maturities ₹12.1613 within short debt, so maturities are not added again. Normalized EBITDA₹59.2640 yields debt/EBITDA1.84× and operating interest cover 8.13×, counterweights to an unsupported default claim. [S1]
Receivables ₹195.1104 represent 172 closing sales-days; average-balance days are 114, explaining the rating's lower number without silently substituting it. About ₹11.0697 crore is over six months, including ₹3.3724 over one year. Predominantly recent invoices do not prove subsequent collection. The auditor identifies milestone/completion revenue and fixed-asset capitalization as key matters. Debtor recoveries, year-end revenue cut-off, inventory ownership/obsolescence and advance recoverability need testing alongside the internal-control finding. [S1, S5]
Operating EBIT is defined consistently as PBT+finance cost−other income; FY26₹57.7431 versus FY25₹15.1466, margins 13.93% versus 6.15%. FY26 deferred-tax credit ₹2.5088 and minority profit ₹2.62 distinguish group PAT from ₹40.1216 attributable to owners. The rating's total-operating-income/EBITDA definitions differ from the financial-statement revenue/normalized EBITDA; both remain identified. Original FY25 cash flow resolves a reversed PPE sign in FY26 comparative presentation. Historical accounting scope, goodwill, property, deposits, noncash flows and corporate guarantees remain visible, not buried in a clean ratio.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Historical current-share P/E is 12.16×, owners' book multiple 4.47×, and an explicitly dated March-debt/excess-cash-above-₹5-crore-floor bridge gives EV/normalized EBITDA10.07×. These are cross-checks, not a current EV: July capital receipts and subsequent expenditure make a mixed-date EV imperfect. Current-share owner earnings are ₹32.54, not reported weighted-average EPS₹33.91 multiplied by the current share count. No investment-property or factory value is added to an operating multiple, and no gross IPO proceeds are added again to cash. [S1, S7, S10]
The embedded model contains every FY27–31 row for bear/base/bull, each ordinary, conditional-warrant and rescue variant. Revenue, EBIT,26% tax, depreciation, ONWC, capex, interest, principal, cash, new equity/warrants/options and final shares are linked. The five-year investor convention is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, using FY31 earnings and modeled 31 March 2031 balances at exit, not measured October 2031 balances; no invented April–October 2031 cash is added. Operating EBIT multiples 8×/12×/16× are assumptions. Dividends are zero and only retained cash above a ₹5 crore operating floor is added once. NCI is explicitly approximated by FY26 minority share of group profit, not claimed as legal uniform subsidiary ownership. [S1, S6, S7, S8]
All ordinary IRRs, ordinary terminal investable prices and ordinary entry prices are null. The cases require cash that is not presently verified. Full future warrant exercise still leaves early gaps. Only a separately labelled rescue assumes new equity at 40% below the reference quote; its proceeds increase cash and its shares increase the denominator simultaneously. The default issuance fee is explicitly zero;2% and 5% gross-proceeds fees are separately tested with full cash/share rows. Those diagnostic returns are not R inputs or price targets. Warrant upfront receipts enter only once, and only remaining 75% is added at future exercise. ESOP proceeds are zero solely as a conservative unknown-terms assumption. Known legacy nontrade/nonadvance liabilities and provisions of ₹20.2817 crore are conservatively paid once in FY27, outside partial ONWC; these include ₹9.4448 crore prior-year tax and ₹0.3728 crore accrued interest. They are not deducted again at exit. No excluded other-current-asset recovery offsets the base funding need. Explicit extra-liability and asset-recovery sensitivities show uncertainty without calling those assets available finance.
Two-way growth/multiple and margin/multiple grids contain complete annual financing rows, with entry sensitivities at 12%,15%,18% hurdles. A linked 30-day collection delay,3-point margin loss and 20% capex overrun increases required rescue and reduces return. Reverse algebra holds terminal capital fixed and is explicitly not a self-financing solution. The apparent upside requires execution and external capital that the present evidence cannot certify. [S1, S5–S8]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not merely multiple compression. Delayed project acceptance or weaker inverter/storage sell-through keeps inventory, receivables and advances outstanding; margin pressure lowers internally generated funds; customers' advances become delivery obligations while suppliers and banks demand cash; capex cannot be stopped without impairment; then warrant holders may not exercise, pledged shares face pressure and fresh equity is required at an adverse price. This can permanently dilute common owners even if the operating company survives. The key falsifiable variable is conversion of reported growth into unrestricted cash after necessary investment, rather than the reported order pipeline. [S1, S5–S8]
In the modeled ordinary bear, the maximum notional gap to a ₹5 crore minimum cash balance is ₹109.06 crore; even full conditional warrants cannot resolve the first-year shortfall. The hypothetical rescue bear produces terminal price around ₹195.29, approximately−50.64% from ₹395.65 and five-year diagnostic IRR−13.17%, before personal taxes and unknown actual market impact. This is not a forecast of actual loss or a solvency conclusion; the case assumes both the recapitalization price and its availability. Unfunded ordinary returns remain null. All annual rows and claims are retained so the reader can inspect how the gap and dilution arise.
Impairment concern is High, owing to uncertain cash accessibility, concentration, pledged supply, expansion commitments and controls. The contrary case is important: positive EBITDA/interest cover, a rating upgrade, July cash raising and new awards could fund successful growth if collections and facility access prove reliable. No severe fraud/default fact has been established. Evidence of completed collection, sound controls and sufficient committed liquidity would reduce this risk; a higher share quote alone would not.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Five-year 5× and 10× price outcomes require approximately 37.97% and 58.49% annualized per-share returns;10× over ten years requires 25.89%. Business revenue growth is not the same as equity value growth or per-share return. Warrants/options alone could increase shares from 12.3298 million to 15.39045 million; any rescue adds further shares. At unchanged net margin and P/E, a 5× per-share result therefore needs substantially more than 5× revenue when shares increase. The model's multiple-normalization bear and conditional financing paths demonstrate the distinction.
These outcomes are classified Speculative/unsupported, not impossible. Accessible customers, saleable capacity, incremental after-tax capital returns and a funded expansion path are not yet demonstrated at the scale required. The group does not disclose enough stable product-volume/unit-price/external-revenue data to derive credible required market share. It would be false precision to turn the 3 GWh nameplate ambition into a 5× target. No success probability, target price or long-range upside ranking is assigned. Strong reported growth is a reason to investigate the economics, not substitute for them. [S1, S6–S8]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Eight company-specific monitoring items are embedded as a structured register. First, reconcile FY26 borrowing-in-CFO and independently evidence uncleared-cheque realization and subsequent receivable recovery. Second, verify September 2026 Dasna full-phase commissioning, qualification, utilization and sold output rather than only ceremonial inauguration. Third, obtain a current group cash/debt/committed-credit and capex-payment bridge; proposed credit and non-fund limits remain excluded. Fourth, track the unpaid warrant subscriptions against December 2026 and January 2028 deadlines without presuming exercise. [S1, S5–S8]
Fifth, reconcile delivery and cash realization of the September microinverter order, November EPC deadline and December tracker awards; include net-of-tax revenue and cancellation/advance terms. Sixth, check age-specific receivables and supplier/customer advances, including whether debtor days fall because revenue accelerated rather than cash arrived. Seventh, review promoter encumbrance, RPT loan settlements and guarantee location alongside control-remediation evidence. Eighth, compare subsequent reported guidance against original dated targets and externally reconciled segment revenue. [S1, S7, S12–S16]
Suggested review is at each material exchange filing and the next financial release, not an autonomous reminder or standing trading action. Thresholds are investigation triggers, not mechanical buy/sell rules: missed cash or commissioning evidence keeps holds in place; demonstrated diversion or unfinanceable obligations would change gates; a normal quote fluctuation would not. Ordinary funding must be established before a supported return case can be promoted out of the rescue appendix.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final research classification: Verification hold / unranked SME expansion case. Business Quality NS, Growth Quality NS and Investment Attractiveness NS at ₹395.65, conditional on an illustrative ₹5 lakh position. Not a confirmed compounder, not a screened-only placeholder, and not Avoid—governance: the dossier completes the required analytical work but the sources leave important evidence genuinely unresolved. GOV4 does not trigger the≤3 override. G3 is an unresolved hold, not an evidenced fail, so no arbitrary 3-point funding cap is substituted for missing IAS. [S1, S5–S10]
For a new investment conclusion, obtain the current cash and undrawn facility bridge, auditor-supported cash-flow/recovery reconciliation and attributable capital-return evidence before evaluating a funded base-case hurdle. For an existing holder, the same questions prioritize information gathering and liquidity planning; this research does not infer the user's actual holdings, risk capacity, sale instruction or suitable position size. The ₹474,780 floor and ₹553,910 ceiling are mechanical 200-share-lot examples, not recommended allocations. [S10]
What changes the view: verified cash realization, effective controls, adequate committed funding without a rescue, repeatable qualified sales and returns on fully loaded new investment. What does not: a larger order announcement alone, a famous counterparty, national TAM, a higher market quote or an unsourced high ROCE. Once material gaps resolve, recompute exactly the same factor weights and gates; do not retrofit a more favorable rubric.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence comprises FY24–FY26 exchange annual reports, the official RHP, May audited results, November/June transcripts, July allotment/shareholding and EGM terms, specific order disclosures, the September rating, and official NSE quote/security/surveillance/holiday archives. Material evidence is tagged V (verified disclosure), C (calculation), M (management statement) or A (assumption). Exact URLs, retrieval dates, locators and original-file hashes are retained in the source ledger. Stable qualitative peer roles are separately labelled; no later-period peer financial numbers influence the cutoff conclusion.
The highest-priority open questions are: current bank cash and cheque collections; financing versus operating cash classification; genuine committed undrawn credit for each borrower; capex already paid versus still committed; external revenue/organic and group eliminations bridge; attributable return on new capital; current ownership/RPT/guarantee exposures; September commissioning and order execution; ESOP terms; and guidance revisions. A negative search is ND, not proof that a disclosure does not exist. Original source PDFs can contain irrelevant private identifiers and are deliberately omitted from delivered backups.
All forward growth, margins, depreciation, normalized tax, WC, capex, exit multiples, minority proxy, rescue price and costs are explicit analytical assumptions. Source-free rebuild establishes deterministic arithmetic and artifact reproduction only. It cannot reauthenticate websites, independently verify underlying issuer claims or turn assumptions into evidence. QA separately distinguishes processed-data checks, locally retained source-file hash checks and model regeneration. This report is research, not a transaction instruction, audited assurance or individualized investment advice.

summary:
Research completed with unresolved verification holds, not a buy recommendation: GP Eco is a rapidly expanding solar distribution/EPC/storage group, but reported profit growth is materially stronger than independently interpretable cash generation. At the 19 October 2026 official close of ₹395.65, current issued-share market value is ₹487.8285 crore. The 20 October cutoff was an NSE cash-market holiday, so no 20 October quote is invented. [S10, S11]
BQS, GQS (Growth Quality Score) and IAS are all NS. Known-weight coverage is 68%,45% and 10%; original-weight mathematical bounds are 3.04–5.92,2.60–7.55 and 1.60–9.70, not estimated scores or confidence intervals. Persistent weak cash conversion would cap a fully computable GQS at 5; it does not turn missing evidence into a 5. No score is ranking-eligible. [S1–S10]
The decisive evidence is the FY26 cash-flow statement: reported CFO₹29.3263 crore includes ₹35.5470 crore of short-term borrowing increase. Subtracting this financing movement produces a diagnostic negative ₹6.2207 crore, not an audited restatement. Moreover,₹14.5967 crore of ₹19.6999 crore reported cash comprises uncleared cheques. The audit's main opinion is unmodified, but its internal-control annex calls for stronger debtor/stock controls. [S1]
Strong counter-evidence exists: revenue grew 68.15%, normalized operating EBIT reached ₹57.7431 crore, the September credit rating improved, July capital was raised and specific new orders were disclosed. Those positives warrant continued research rather than an allegation of fraud/default. They do not establish current usable funds or attributable returns on new capital. An apparently 12.16× historical earnings quote therefore does not establish a bargain. [S1, S5, S7, S12–S15]
